correctness.rationale: Each directed first-passage time equals the sum of holding-time means 1/r_i along the sole directed path, so the longest paths omit precisely one edge and the objective is sum_i 1/r_i−min_j 1/r_j. For arbitrary probability q on omitted edges, max >=sum_i(1−q_i)/r_i >=(sum_i sqrt(c_i(1−q_i)))² by price-budget Cauchy–Schwarz. Maximizing the concave dual over q yields KKT q_i=(1−c_i/theta)_+, unique theta, and at least two positive q_i; equality produces all strictly positive optimal rates with clipped inverse-square-root prices. Strict equality under Cauchy–Schwarz gives uniqueness. Direct algebra checks example c=(1,3,100), theta=4,Z=12,r=(1/24,1/24,1/120), max=144, and equal-rate max=208. Independently checked the source Poisson-generator verifier, exact threshold relation, and numerical feasible comparisons; the universal claim rests on the analytic minimax lower-bound/equality proof.

originality.rationale: Previously published surveillance optimization works focus on stationary-weighted average hitting time, cyclic observation gaps, or general discrete-time largest MFPT bounds. The closest Breen–Kirkland paper treats maximum MFPT but in a different discrete-time optimization/normalization and does not provide the arbitrary positive price clipped law in inspected sections. Resultary search located no direct equivalent result. Prior specialized priced-cycle formula could still exist.

value.rationale: A complete analytic solution to a natural continuous-time network design minimax problem with arbitrary positive linear rate prices, identifying a nontrivial clipped threshold and a sharp uniform-rate phase, provides an interpretable and practically reusable allocation law, not just a routine uniform-rate exercise.

final_claim: For a positively priced one-way continuous-time n-cycle (n>=3), the unique minimizer of the maximum distinct-state mean first-passage time is r_i=1/(Z sqrt(max(c_i,theta))), where theta solves sum(1-c_i/theta)_+=1 and Z=sum c_i/sqrt(max(c_i,theta)); optimum equals Z².
limitations: Analytical uniqueness uses positive costs and unbounded positive rates subject to a single linear budget.
No claim for arbitrary directed graphs, cover times, spectral gaps or fixed stationary distributions.
An older specialized resource-allocation law for one-way stochastic cycles may have been published under a dual optimization name.
The model excludes bidirectional arcs, rate caps, stationary constraints, and same-state return times.
